newsitem.title: CHINA: China firms make compliance strides - HK bourse.
newsitem.headline: China firms make compliance strides - HK bourse.

text.p: Chinese firms listed in Hong Kong have room for improvement in compliance with the territory's regulations but the stock exchange is pleased with progress overall, Hong Kong bourse chairman Edgar Cheng said.
"The stock exchange is very pleased with the developmental progress in the H share listings," Cheng told reporters after a seminar in Beijing on Thursday.
H shares refer to Chinese companies that are traded on the Hong Kong market.
Many analysts have complained of lack of transparency in the operations of some H share companies.
Some Hong Kong-listed firms have also come under fire for using proceeds from public offers for purposes not stated in their offer prospectus.
"There is room for improvement," he said, referring to compliance issues in general.
"This (process) started three years ago and we have come a long way," he said, adding that annual and half-year reports were an area of particular progress so far.
"I believe that over time they (Chinese companies) will be able to satisfy these (compliance) demands," he said.
